# llms.txt - Machine-Readable Context for LSH
# https://github.com/gwicho38/lsh
# For ML models/agents to quickly understand this CLI tool
# This file IS the machine-readable context — there is no `lsh context` command in v4. Read it directly: `cat llms.txt`

> LSH is an encrypted secrets manager for .env files with cloud sync via IPFS/Storacha.

## Quick Context

Name: lsh (lsh-framework on npm)
Purpose: Encrypted secrets manager with multi-host sync
Install: npm install -g lsh-framework
Repository: https://github.com/gwicho38/lsh
Docs: https://github.com/gwicho38/lsh/blob/main/README.md

## v4.0.0 Breaking Change

The CLI surface is now five commands plus `help`: `push`, `pull`, `sync`, `edit`, `list`. Every other v3 top-level
command was removed. Running a removed command prints its exact v4 replacement. See
[docs/releases/4.0.0.md](docs/releases/4.0.0.md) for the full removal table.

## Primary Use Case

Sync .env files across development machines with AES-256 encryption:
1. Generate encryption key once: `lsh sync --init`
2. Push secrets to cloud: `lsh push`
3. Pull on another machine: `lsh pull`

## Command Reference

### Setup Commands (First-Time)
lsh sync --init                   # Interactive setup wizard (installs IPFS, generates a key)
lsh sync --key                    # Print the effective encryption key
lsh sync --key=<value>            # Import/persist a shared encryption key
lsh sync --doctor                 # Verify configuration and connectivity

### Core Secrets Commands
lsh push [--env <name>] [--file <path>]    # Upload encrypted .env to cloud
lsh pull [--env <name>] [--file <path>]    # Download .env from cloud
lsh sync                                    # Smart sync (push or pull, whichever is newer)
lsh list                                    # List local secrets (env format, masked)
lsh list --format json|yaml|toml|export     # List local secrets (unmasked — for eval/jq/etc.)
lsh list --no-mask                          # Force real values in the env format
lsh list --keys-only                        # List only key names
lsh edit --get --all --format <type>        # List local secrets, unmasked (via edit)
lsh sync --status                           # Detailed sync status report

### Individual Secret Operations
lsh edit --get <key>                  # Get specific secret value (unmasked)
lsh edit --set <key>=<value>          # Set specific secret value
rm .env                               # Delete .env file
lsh edit                              # Open .env in $EDITOR (creates it if missing)

### Multi-Environment Support
lsh push --env dev                    # Push to dev environment
lsh push --env staging                # Push to staging environment
lsh push --env prod                   # Push to production environment
lsh pull --env prod                   # Pull from production
lsh push --file .env.local --env local  # Custom file to custom env

### IPFS / Sync Commands
lsh sync --doctor                     # Check local Kubo (IPFS) node + install status
lsh sync                              # Sync secrets via IPFS (push/pull as needed)
lsh sync --history                    # View immutable sync records stored on IPFS

The IPFS daemon itself is managed automatically — `push`, `pull`, and `sync` each install Kubo if
missing and start the daemon if it isn't running. There is no separate start/stop command.

### Configuration
lsh sync --config                     # Print the resolved configuration and its source path

### Version / Update
npm install -g lsh-framework          # Update to latest version
lsh --version                         # Show version
lsh --help                            # Show help

## Common Patterns

### First-Time Setup on Any Machine
```bash
npm install -g lsh-framework
lsh sync --init              # Interactive setup
lsh sync --doctor            # Verify everything works
```

### Daily Developer Workflow
```bash
cd ~/repos/my-project
lsh pull                    # Get latest secrets
# ... work ...
lsh push                    # Push any changes
```

### Team Onboarding
```bash
# Team lead shares LSH_SECRETS_KEY via 1Password
echo "LSH_SECRETS_KEY=shared-key" >> .env
lsh pull --env prod
```

### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# In GitHub Actions / CI pipeline:
export LSH_SECRETS_KEY=${{ secrets.LSH_SECRETS_KEY }}
lsh pull --env $ENVIRONMENT
source .env
```

### Automatic Secret Rotation
# Rotation is driven by your own scheduler (system cron, CI job) — not a built-in daemon.
```bash
# Example crontab entry (crontab -e): monthly rotate + push
0 0 1 * * cd /path/to/project && ./scripts/rotate.sh && lsh push
```

## Environment Variables

### Required
LSH_SECRETS_KEY=<64-char-hex>         # AES-256 encryption key (from `lsh sync --init`)

### Optional
LSH_PIN_SERVICE=<service-name>        # Kubo remote pinning service for durable sync

## File Locations

~/.config/lsh/lshrc                   # Global LSH configuration
~/.lsh/secrets-cache/                 # Encrypted secrets cache
~/.lsh/secrets-metadata.json          # Metadata index
.env                                  # Local environment file (default)

## Exit Codes

0 - Success
1 - General error (check stderr for details)

## Output Formats

lsh edit --get --all --format env     # KEY=value (default)
lsh edit --get --all --format json    # {"KEY": "value"}
lsh edit --get --all --format yaml    # KEY: value
lsh edit --get --all --format toml    # KEY = "value"
lsh edit --get --all --format export  # export KEY='value' (shell-sourceable)

## Error Resolution

### "No secrets found for environment"
Run `lsh edit --get --all --format env` to see what's in your local .env, then
`lsh push --env <name>` to create the environment on first push.

### "Decryption failed"
Ensure LSH_SECRETS_KEY matches the key used to encrypt. Generate a new key with `lsh sync --init` if lost.

### "IPFS daemon not running" / sync hangs or fails
`push`, `pull`, and `sync` install and start the local Kubo node automatically — run
`lsh sync --doctor` to diagnose, or `lsh sync --status` for current state. For durable pulls,
configure a remote pinning service (see README "Durable sync").

## Security Model

- AES-256-CBC encryption (local)
- Content-addressed IPFS storage (tamper-proof)
- Zero-knowledge: only encrypted blobs leave the machine; no server sees plaintext
- Keys never transmitted, only encrypted blobs

## Integration Points

### Load Secrets into Shell
```bash
eval "$(lsh sync --load)"
```

### Load Specific Secret
```bash
API_KEY=$(lsh edit --get API_KEY)
```

### Check if Synced
```bash
lsh sync --status --format json
```

## For ML Agents

This file (`llms.txt`) is the full machine-readable context for LSH — there is no separate
`lsh context` command in v4.0.0. Read it directly:
```bash
cat llms.txt
```
